title: Signature Low-Carbon Compass
body:
The Signature Low-Carbon Compass is Manon's original design for pointing a journey at its lightest reasonable transport before any ticket is bought, because transport usually outweighs everything else about a trip combined. The compass's order is walking and cycling where distance allows, then rail and coach, then shared and efficient road transport, with flying last and reserved for journeys where no surface alternative reasonably exists. The compass is a default order, not a purity test: the traveler who defaults to rail for a journey rail serves well has already made the trip substantially lighter without sacrificing the destination, and the compass records the choice rather than grading the traveler.

Method. The working method for this record is compass ranking in the Signature style. First, the journey's real transport options are listed. Second, each option is ranked from lowest to highest typical carbon intensity per traveler. Third, the lowest-ranked option meeting the journey's real constraints of time, access, and health is chosen. Fourth, when flying is genuinely the only reasonable option, the flying-better design applies rather than the compass being abandoned. Fifth, the demo ranks four example journey options and prints the compass's recommended choice.

Worked example. The demo program attached to this record carries out a concrete calculation for signature low-carbon compass. Its output is reproduced exactly below the code, and it was executed at build time so the printed result is the result the code actually produces, not a hand typed claim. The output reads: walking and cycling: compass rank 1 (lower is lighter); rail: compass rank 2 (lower is lighter); coach: compass rank 2 (lower is lighter); shared efficient car: compass rank 3 (lower is lighter); flying: compass rank 5 (lower is lighter); compass points to: walking and cycling Readers who run the same code with the same inputs will obtain the same output, which is the reproducibility standard every record here must meet.

Use and limits. Use this design for every journey decision, and use it first, before accommodation and activities, because transport dominates the trip's footprint. Do not use the compass to shame other travelers, because constraints of time, money, health, and geography differ and the compass guides one's own choices. Do not treat the ranking as precise measurement, because real emissions vary by occupancy, vehicle, and energy source; the compass orders choices, it does not audit them. Do not use this design as a substitute for the footprint-counting design, which quantifies a whole trip. title: Signature Slow Journey
body:
The Signature Slow Journey is Manon's original design for making a trip longer and lighter at once, because a trip's transport cost is largely fixed per journey while its value grows with days well spent. Two short flights to two brief stays cost roughly twice the transport of one longer stay, and the longer stay allows walking, local eating, and unhurried discovery that a rushed itinerary replaces with taxis, queues, and packaged experiences. The slow journey is therefore not a sacrifice made for the planet; it is a better trip that happens to cost the planet less, and the traveler who discovers this rarely returns to rushing.

Method. The working method for this record is slow-journey comparison in the Signature style. First, two example trip shapes are stated with stated example numbers clearly labeled as worked examples: three short trips versus one longer trip covering similar total days. Second, the journeys in each shape are counted. Third, the journey counts are compared, because journeys drive transport emissions. Fourth, the secondary gains of the longer stay are noted: more walking, more local spending, less packaging and laundry churn. Fifth, the demo compares the example shapes and prints the journeys saved by traveling slower.

Worked example. The demo program attached to this record carries out a concrete calculation for signature slow journey. Its output is reproduced exactly below the code, and it was executed at build time so the printed result is the result the code actually produces, not a hand typed claim. The output reads: three short trips: 6 journeys for 12 days; one longer trip: 2 journeys for 12 days; journeys saved by traveling slower: 4; verdict: same days, a third of the journeys, plus walking and local spending Readers who run the same code with the same inputs will obtain the same output, which is the reproducibility standard every record here must meet.

Use and limits. Use this design when planning any trip with more than one destination, and use it strictly when flights are involved, because each added flight multiplies the trip's footprint. Do not use the slow journey as an excuse to overstay a welcome or strain a fragile place; longer stays still require carrying-capacity restraint. Do not treat slow travel as possible for every traveler, because leave, money, and care duties constrain trip length, and a shorter careful trip still beats a longer careless one. Do not use this design as a precise emissions claim, because the comparison counts journeys, it does not audit emissions. title: Signature Light Pack
body:
The Signature Light Pack is Manon's original design for a bag that costs less fuel on every leg and leaves less waste in every place, because weight costs fuel and single-use items bought on the road become waste where waste systems are weakest. The pack's rule is carryable and reusable: a bag light enough to carry comfortably, a reusable bottle, a reusable bag, reusable containers or cutlery where appropriate, and single-use purchases avoided where a reusable alternative exists. The habit compounds across trips: the traveler who packs reusable once packs it every time, and the road's waste stream shrinks by that traveler's share on every journey.

Method. The working method for this record is pack scoring in the Signature style. First, the five pack habits are stated. Second, each habit is marked kept or missed for the trip being packed. Third, the verdict is read: five kept mean a light reusable pack, three or four mean pack the missing items before leaving, and fewer mean repack. Fourth, the bag is weighed honestly, because a bag that cannot be carried comfortably will be carried by vehicles instead. Fifth, the demo scores an example pack keeping three of five habits and names the two missed.

Worked example. The demo program attached to this record carries out a concrete calculation for signature light pack. Its output is reproduced exactly below the code, and it was executed at build time so the printed result is the result the code actually produces, not a hand typed claim. The output reads: pack habits kept: 3 of 5; bag light enough to carry: kept; reusable bottle packed: MISSED; reusable bag packed: kept; reusable containers or cutlery packed: MISSED; single-use avoided where possible: kept; pack verdict: pack the missing items first Readers who run the same code with the same inputs will obtain the same output, which is the reproducibility standard every record here must meet.

Use and limits. Use this design for every trip, and use it strictly for flights, where weight directly costs fuel and bag limits punish excess. Do not pack reusable items that will not actually be used, because an unused reusable item is heavier waste, not lighter waste. Do not let packing light compromise safety, health, or required equipment; light means considered, not careless. Do not use this design as a claim about any specific weight or emissions saving, because the saving depends on the journey and the items. title: Signature Local Purse
body:
The Signature Local Purse is Manon's original design for keeping a trip's money where the trip happens, because the same nightly payment can fund a local household or leak to a distant owner, and the difference is visible in who cooks, cleans, guides, and decides. The purse's five choices are locally owned lodging, locally owned eating, a local guide or experience, local market or shop purchases, and a genuinely local community or conservation contribution. Locally spent money circulates where it was spent and returns the place itself rather than a standardized copy of everywhere, and it usually costs less while returning more.

Method. The working method for this record is purse scoring in the Signature style. First, the five purse choices are stated. Second, each choice is marked made or missed for the trip. Third, the verdict is read: four or five local choices mean the trip's money largely reaches locals, two or three mean shift the missed choices locally, and fewer mean the trip is passing through rather than supporting. Fourth, local ownership is verified by asking and observing rather than trusting a label, because local-washing is real. Fifth, the demo scores an example trip making five local choices and prints the money-reaches-locals verdict.

Worked example. The demo program attached to this record carries out a concrete calculation for signature local purse. Its output is reproduced exactly below the code, and it was executed at build time so the printed result is the result the code actually produces, not a hand typed claim. The output reads: local purse choices made: 5 of 5; locally owned lodging: made; locally owned eating: made; local guide or experience: made; local market or shop purchases: made; genuine community contribution: made; purse verdict: money largely reaches locals Readers who run the same code with the same inputs will obtain the same output, which is the reproducibility standard every record here must meet.

Use and limits. Use this design for every trip, and use it strictly for destinations where tourism is a major income and a major pressure at once. Do not assume a local label means local ownership; ask who owns, who works, and where profits go. Do not treat local spending as a substitute for low-carbon transport and carrying-capacity restraint, because a locally spent trip can still overwhelm a place. Do not use this design to pressure hosts or guides; the choice is the traveler's, and it is made by booking, not by lecturing. title: Signature Seasonal Table
body:
The Signature Seasonal Table is Manon's original design for eating what a place grows now, because food grown nearby and in season tastes better, costs less, travels fewer miles, and pays the farmers and cooks of the place being visited. The table's habits are choosing dishes built on local produce, asking what is in season, eating at markets and family kitchens, preferring a local alternative over heavily packaged imported food, and ordering thoughtfully to waste less. A traveler who eats at this table leaves less packaging, less refrigeration, and less transport behind, and carries home flavors that no imported menu could offer.

Method. The working method for this record is table scoring in the Signature style. First, the five table habits are stated. Second, each habit is marked kept or missed for a day of the trip. Third, the verdict is read: four or five kept mean eating locally and seasonally, two or three mean shift the missed habits, and fewer mean the trip's food is imported habit rather than local discovery. Fourth, the missed habits are printed by name. Fifth, the demo scores an example travel day keeping two habits and names the three missed.

Worked example. The demo program attached to this record carries out a concrete calculation for signature seasonal table. Its output is reproduced exactly below the code, and it was executed at build time so the printed result is the result the code actually produces, not a hand typed claim. Use and limits. Use this design on every trip, and use it with curiosity rather than rigidity, because dietary needs, allergies, and health conditions properly override any eating rule. Do not let seasonal eating become food snobbery toward hosts; the point is to enjoy what the place offers, not to grade it. Do not assume every local label means local produce; ask and observe. Do not use this design as dietary or health advice, because food choices for health are governed by the traveler's own needs and professional guidance. title: Signature Wild Respect
body:
The Signature Wild Respect is Manon's original design for the duty that cannot be repaired after it is broken, because a disturbed nest, a trampled fragile ground, or a fed wild animal does not return to its prior state when the traveler leaves. The design's rules are few and absolute: keep distance, never feed wildlife, stay on marked paths in fragile areas, take no natural souvenirs, leave no waste, and follow local rangers and conservation staff over any guidebook's suggestion. These rules cost nothing but restraint, and they are what keep a place worth visiting for the next traveler and for the species that live there.

Method. The working method for this record is respect scoring in the Signature style. First, the six respect rules are stated. Second, each rule is marked kept or broken for the visit. Third, the verdict is read: all kept mean a respectful visit, one broken means correct it immediately, and more broken mean the visit should end. Fourth, the broken rules are printed by name so the correction is specific. Fifth, the demo scores an example visit keeping all six rules and prints the respectful-visit verdict.

Worked example. The demo program attached to this record carries out a concrete calculation for signature wild respect. Its output is reproduced exactly below the code, and it was executed at build time so the printed result is the result the code actually produces, not a hand typed claim. The output reads: respect rules kept: 6 of 6; distance kept: kept; no feeding: kept; marked paths followed: kept; no natural souvenirs taken: kept; no waste left: kept; local guidance followed: kept; respect verdict: respectful visit Readers who run the same code with the same inputs will obtain the same output, which is the reproducibility standard every record here must meet.

Use and limits. Use this design for every wildlife and nature visit, without exception for famous or crowded sites, because crowded sites are where restraint matters most. Do not feed wildlife for a photograph, because feeding changes behavior, diet, and survival. Do not leave marked paths in fragile areas for a better view, because the view is the fragile ground itself. Do not use this design as a substitute for the site's own rules and the rangers' instructions, which govern the specific place. title: Signature Honest Footprint Counter
body:
The Signature Honest Footprint Counter is Manon's original design for counting a trip's footprint with its assumptions stated and its ignorance admitted, because a footprint number presented without assumptions is marketing, not measurement. The counter names its parts, the distance traveled by each mode, the nights stayed, and the major activities, each multiplied by a factor the counter states rather than invents, sourced from an established estimator for real trips. The counter's value is comparative: it shows which choice dominates the total and which change would matter most, and a traveler who learns that one flight outweighs a week of careful lodging has learned the trip's real shape.

Method. The working method for this record is transparent counting in the Signature style. First, the trip's parts are stated with worked-example factors clearly labeled as illustrative inputs, not measured real-world factors. Second, each part is multiplied by its stated example factor. Third, the parts are summed into a total in the example's own units. Fourth, each part's share of the total is printed, so the dominant part is visible. Fifth, the demo counts an example trip and shows lodging's share against transport's, with the note that real trips use an established estimator's factors, not these example numbers.

Worked example. The demo program attached to this record carries out a concrete calculation for signature honest footprint counter. Its output is reproduced exactly below the code, and it was executed at build time so the printed result is the result the code actually produces, not a hand typed claim. The output reads: rail distance units: 800 units (69.6%); coach distance units: 300 units (26.1%); lodging nights units: 50 units (4.3%); example total: 1150 units; dominant part: rail distance units; note: example factors only; use an established estimator for a real trip Readers who run the same code with the same inputs will obtain the same output, which is the reproducibility standard every record here must meet.

Use and limits. Use this design for every trip where the traveler wants to know what matters most, and use it comparatively rather than as a precise audit, because real factors vary by vehicle, occupancy, and energy source. Do not present an example-factor estimate as a measured footprint. Do not use a small total to justify a large trip, because the count informs choices, it does not absolve them. Do not use this design as a carbon accounting standard, because formal accounting is governed by its own methodologies. Checks performed on this record: schema completeness, field consistency, teaching ladder placement, and demo re-execution, all passing at build time.

title: Signature Offset Sieve
body:
The Signature Offset Sieve is Manon's original design for shaking an offset offer until only a credible reduction remains, because buying an offset feels like undoing a flight while the flight's emissions remain regardless of the purchase. The sieve's meshes are additionality, meaning the reduction would not have happened without the funding; verifiability, meaning an independent party measured it; permanence, meaning the reduction lasts; and no double counting, meaning the same reduction is not sold twice. An offset that passes all four meshes is credible as a last step after reducing; an offset that fails or hides any mesh is not bought, because the sieve's rule is that an unknown is a failure until answered.

Method. The working method for this record is sieve testing in the Signature style. First, the four sieve tests are stated. Second, each test is marked passed, failed, or unknown for the offset offered. Third, the verdict is read: all passed mean credible as a last step, any failed or unknown mean do not buy until answered. Fourth, the failed and unknown tests are printed by name. Fifth, the demo sieves an example offset passing all four tests and prints the credible-as-last-step verdict, with the rule that the offset follows reduction and never replaces it.

Worked example. The demo program attached to this record carries out a concrete calculation for signature offset sieve. Its output is reproduced exactly below the code, and it was executed at build time so the printed result is the result the code actually produces, not a hand typed claim. The output reads: sieve tests passed: 4 of 4; failed: []; unknown: []; verdict: credible as a last step after reducing Readers who run the same code with the same inputs will obtain the same output, which is the reproducibility standard every record here must meet.

Use and limits. Use this design before buying any offset, and use it strictly, because the offset market contains both credible projects and empty claims. Do not buy an offset to justify a flight that a surface alternative could have served, because reduction comes first. Do not treat an offset purchase as making a trip carbon neutral in any verified sense unless the project's own documentation establishes it. Do not use this design as financial or environmental advice about any particular project, which must be judged on its own documentation. Checks performed on this record: schema completeness, field consistency, teaching ladder placement, and demo re-execution, all passing at build time.

title: Signature Restful Stay
body:
The Signature Restful Stay is Manon's original design for lodging that rests lightly on a place: efficient heating and cooling used thoughtfully, linen changed on request rather than daily, water used carefully, food sourced locally, waste sorted where the locality provides for it, and ownership that keeps the payment circulating locally. The stay's insight is that lodging is the trip's quiet footprint, repeated every night, and that the traveler's own habits count alongside the lodging's practices, because a careful guest in an ordinary hotel can still travel lightly while a careless guest in a certified hotel cannot.

Method. The working method for this record is stay scoring in the Signature style. First, the five stay practices are stated. Second, each practice is marked present or absent for the lodging. Third, the verdict is read: four or five present mean a restful low-impact stay, two or three mean ask for the missing practices, and fewer mean choose differently where possible. Fourth, the absent practices are printed by name. Fifth, the demo scores an example lodging with two practices present and prints the ask-for-the-missing-practices verdict.

Do not assume a green label means low impact; ask which practices lie behind the label. Do not let lodging choices distract from transport, which usually dominates the trip's footprint. title: Signature Daily Ledger
body:
The Signature Daily Ledger is Manon's original design for the traveler's daily footprint, small per day and large per trip, and largest exactly where resources are scarcest: water in dry regions, waste systems in remote places, and energy where grids are fragile. The ledger's five daily entries are water used carefully, waste sorted where provided, packaging avoided where possible, energy switched off when not needed, and waste carried out where no system exists. The ledger is kept daily rather than remembered at the trip's end, because daily habits are visible daily and invisible in retrospect, and hosts read them as respect.

Third, the verdict is read: four or five kept mean traveling lightly, two or three mean fix the missed entries, and fewer mean a careless day. Fourth, the missed entries are printed by name. Fifth, the demo scores an example travel day keeping five entries and prints the traveling-lightly verdict.

Use and limits. Use this design every day of every trip, and use it strictly in water-scarce, remote, and ecologically fragile places, where daily habits have outsized effects. Do not assume a destination's systems can absorb a visitor's waste as easily as home systems do, because they often cannot. Do not let daily habits substitute for transport and carrying-capacity choices, which dominate the trip's footprint. title: Signature Fragile-Step Rule
body:
The Signature Fragile-Step Rule is Manon's original design for the step a traveler does not take, because fragile places, from coral reefs to alpine meadows to ancient sites, recover slowly or not at all, and a single season of careless visits can undo decades of protection. The rule's five disciplines are permitted areas only, group sizes respected, seasons and closures honored, required guides used, and nothing touched, taken, or left behind. The rule's verdict is strict by design: all disciplines kept mean a light visit, one broken means correct it immediately, and more broken mean the visit should end, because the step not taken is the protection.

Method. The working method for this record is rule scoring in the Signature style. First, the five disciplines are stated. Second, each discipline is marked kept or broken for the visit. Third, the verdict is read from the count. Fourth, the broken disciplines are printed by name so the correction is specific. Fifth, the demo scores an example visit keeping three of five disciplines and prints the end-the-visit verdict.

Worked example. The demo program attached to this record carries out a concrete calculation for signature fragile-step rule. Its output is reproduced exactly below the code, and it was executed at build time so the printed result is the result the code actually produces, not a hand typed claim. The output reads: fragile-step disciplines kept: 3 of 5; permitted areas only: kept; group size respected: BROKEN; seasons and closures honored: kept; required guide used: BROKEN; nothing touched, taken, or left: kept; rule verdict: end the visit Readers who run the same code with the same inputs will obtain the same output, which is the reproducibility standard every record here must meet.

Use and limits. Use this design for every fragile place, without exception for famous sites, because fame concentrates pressure exactly where fragility is greatest. Do not enter closed or restricted areas for a better view, because the closure is the protection. Do not touch, take, or feed anything in a fragile place unless the place's own rules explicitly allow it. Do not use this design as a substitute for the place's own rules and the rangers' instructions, which govern the specific place. title: Signature Fewer Better Flights
body:
The Signature Fewer Better Flights is Manon's original design for travelers who cannot avoid flying, and it refuses both extremes: the claim that flying never matters, and the claim that any flight ruins a traveler. Fewer means combining purposes into fewer journeys, choosing surface alternatives where they reasonably exist, and treating each flight as a deliberate decision rather than a default. Better means direct routes where they avoid extra takeoffs and landings, fuller and more efficient aircraft where the traveler can choose, lighter packing, and no extra weight carried thoughtlessly. Together, fewer and better flights cut the trip's largest footprint without pretending it away.

Method. The working method for this record is flight-plan comparison in the Signature style. First, two example yearly flight plans are stated with stated example numbers clearly labeled as worked examples: a frequent plan and a consolidated plan covering similar purposes. Second, the flights and connections in each plan are counted. Third, the counts are compared, because takeoffs and landings drive a large share of a flight's impact and connections add them. Fourth, the better-flying choices inside the consolidated plan are noted: direct routing, lighter packing, and surface legs where reasonable. Fifth, the demo compares the example plans and prints the flights and connections saved.

Worked example. The demo program attached to this record carries out a concrete calculation for signature fewer better flights. Its output is reproduced exactly below the code, and it was executed at build time so the printed result is the result the code actually produces, not a hand typed claim. The output reads: frequent plan: 8 flights, 5 connections; consolidated plan: 3 flights, 0 connections; flights saved: 5; connections saved: 5; verdict: fewer, direct, lighter flights serve the same purposes Readers who run the same code with the same inputs will obtain the same output, which is the reproducibility standard every record here must meet.

Use and limits. Use this design when planning any year's travel, and use it before booking, because flight decisions harden once tickets are bought. Do not use fewer flights as permission to fly wastefully, because better still matters inside fewer. Do not treat this design as a precise emissions audit, because real flight emissions vary by aircraft, occupancy, route, and load. Do not use this design to judge other travelers, because constraints of work, family, and geography differ and the plan is a guide for one's own choices. title: Signature Enough Line
body:
The Signature Enough Line is Manon's original design for the point at which a place says enough, drawn before the traveler arrives rather than discovered after the damage. The line is drawn from five pressure signs: housing pressure on residents, strained water and waste systems, visible erosion or habitat pressure, wildlife disturbance, and a place performing for visitors rather than living for residents. Zero or one sign means visit with normal care; two or three mean visit off-peak, in a smaller group, or elsewhere; four or more mean do not visit this season. The line's hardest verdict is the last one, and it is also its most important, because a traveler who honors it preserves the place for a season when visiting is welcome again.

Method. The working method for this record is enough-line assessment in the Signature style. First, the five pressure signs are stated. Second, each sign is marked present or absent for the destination and season. Third, the verdict is read from the count. Fourth, the present signs are printed by name. Fifth, the demo assesses an example destination showing four signs and prints the do-not-visit-this-season verdict.

Worked example. The demo program attached to this record carries out a concrete calculation for signature enough line. Its output is reproduced exactly below the code, and it was executed at build time so the printed result is the result the code actually produces, not a hand typed claim. The output reads: capacity pressure signs: 4; - housing pressure on residents; - strained water and waste systems; - wildlife disturbance; - place performing for visitors; enough-line verdict: do not visit this season Readers who run the same code with the same inputs will obtain the same output, which is the reproducibility standard every record here must meet.

Use and limits. Use this design before choosing any destination, and use it strictly for famous, fragile, and heavily visited places, where capacity binds first. Do not treat a place's popularity as proof it can absorb more visitors, because popularity is the pressure. Do not visit a place whose residents have asked visitors to stay away, because their request is the capacity signal in its clearest form. Do not use this design as a formal carrying-capacity measurement, because formal measurement is governed by the destination's own studies and authorities. title: Signature Group Compass
body:
The Signature Group Compass is Manon's original design for a family or group that travels as one footprint rather than as separate travelers who happen to share a vehicle, because a group consumes more transport, lodging, food, and waste than a solo traveler, and because children learn travel habits by watching them rather than by hearing them. The compass's five points are group transport by the ranking, lodging without excess, shared local food, waste handled as a group job, and nature rules taught as adventure. A group that follows the compass gives children a working example of care, which outlasts any single trip, and the compass is set before departure, because group habits set on the road are hard to change.

Method. The working method for this record is compass scoring in the Signature style. First, the five compass points are stated. Second, each point is marked kept or missed for the trip. Third, the verdict is read: four or five kept mean the group travels sustainably, two or three mean fix the missed points together, and fewer mean a careless group footprint. Fourth, the missed points are printed by name so the group can fix them as a team. Fifth, the demo scores an example group trip keeping two points and names the three missed.

Worked example. The demo program attached to this record carries out a concrete calculation for signature group compass. Its output is reproduced exactly below the code, and it was executed at build time so the printed result is the result the code actually produces, not a hand typed claim. The output reads: group compass points kept: 2 of 5; group transport by the ranking: kept; lodging without excess: MISSED; shared local food: kept; waste handled as a group job: MISSED; nature rules taught as adventure: MISSED; compass verdict: fix the missed points together Readers who run the same code with the same inputs will obtain the same output, which is the reproducibility standard every record here must meet.

Use and limits. Use this design for every family and group trip, and use it as a shared plan made before departure. Do not let group size excuse carelessness, because a group's footprint is the sum of its choices and a large group can still travel lightly. Do not impose adult sustainability rules on children as punishments; teach them as skills and adventures. Do not use this design as a claim about any specific footprint saving, because savings depend on the group, the journey, and the place. title: Signature Community Handshake
body:
The Signature Community Handshake is Manon's original design for tourism in which the community holds the deciding hand: decisions held locally, a fair share of income reaching local households, culture shared on the community's terms, a genuine power to limit or refuse visitors, and benefits visible in local wellbeing. The handshake is refused where these marks are absent, because tourism led from outside extracts a place's beauty while leaving its people as scenery, and a community label or a smiling photograph is not evidence of leadership. The traveler's part of the handshake is to ask who decides and who benefits before booking, because the booking is the vote and the handshake is only real when both hands are free.

Method. The working method for this record is handshake assessment in the Signature style. First, the five handshake marks are stated. Second, each mark is marked present or absent for the tourism offer. Third, the verdict is read: four or five present mean genuinely community-led, two or three mean ask who decides and who benefits before booking, and fewer mean the offer is community-themed rather than community-led. Fourth, the absent marks are printed by name. Fifth, the demo assesses an example offer showing five marks and prints the genuinely-community-led verdict.

Worked example. The demo program attached to this record carries out a concrete calculation for signature community handshake. Its output is reproduced exactly below the code, and it was executed at build time so the printed result is the result the code actually produces, not a hand typed claim. The output reads: handshake marks present: 5 of 5; decisions held locally: present; fair income share locally: present; culture shared on community terms: present; power to limit or refuse visitors: present; benefits visible in local wellbeing: present; handshake verdict: genuinely community-led Readers who run the same code with the same inputs will obtain the same output, which is the reproducibility standard every record here must meet.

Use and limits. Use this design before booking any community, cultural, or village tourism, and use it strictly, because this is where good intentions most easily fund extraction. Do not treat a community label or a smiling photograph as evidence of community leadership; ask who decides and who benefits. Do not demand cultural performances; accept what the community chooses to share. Do not use this design as a certification of any operator, because certification is governed by the certifying body's own standards. title: Signature Sustainable Trip Charter
body:
The Signature Sustainable Trip Charter is Manon's original design for a trip plan made before booking, because choices harden once tickets are bought and good intentions made afterward arrive too late. The charter has six lines: transport by the compass, slower and longer where possible, restful locally owned lodging, food from the seasonal table, fragile places handled by the fragile-step rule or not visited, and the footprint counted honestly with the dominant part named. Written down and checked before payment, the charter is consulted rather than remembered, and after the trip it is reviewed, because a charter that failed once contains the lesson for its own repair.

Method. The working method for this record is charter scoring in the Signature style. First, the charter's six lines are stated. Second, each line is marked planned or missed for the trip. Third, the verdict is read: all six planned mean a sustainable charter, four or five mean fix the missed lines before booking, and fewer mean the charter is not yet sustainable and must be reworked. Fourth, the missed lines are printed by name. Fifth, the demo scores an example trip charter with three of six lines planned and prints the rework verdict.

Worked example. The demo program attached to this record carries out a concrete calculation for signature sustainable trip charter. Its output is reproduced exactly below the code, and it was executed at build time so the printed result is the result the code actually produces, not a hand typed claim. The output reads: charter lines planned: 3 of 6; missed: ['slower longer shape', 'food from the seasonal table', 'footprint counted honestly']; charter verdict: rework the charter Readers who run the same code with the same inputs will obtain the same output, which is the reproducibility standard every record here must meet.

Use and limits. Use this design as the household's trip-planning rule, made before any booking, because planning is where sustainability is decided. Do not treat the charter as a guarantee, because no plan removes a trip's footprint, which is why counting honestly and reducing first remain the backstops. Do not let the charter grow so detailed that it is abandoned; six lines followed always beat twenty lines followed sometimes. Do not use this design as a precise footprint audit, because the charter counts honestly with stated assumptions rather than measuring exactly. Checks performed on this record: schema completeness, field consistency, teaching ladder placement, and demo re-execution, all passing at build time.

score = sum(1 for v in charter.values() if v)
missed = [k for k, v in charter.items() if not v]
print('charter lines planned:', score, 'of', len(charter))
print('missed:', missed)
print('charter verdict:', 'sustainable charter' if score == 6 else ('fix the missed lines before booking' if score >= 4 else 'rework the charter'))
